title: Bringing agents onto the world wide web — Paul Klein IV, Browserbase
talk_summary: Paul Klein of Browserbase argues that reliable web/browser agents are an engineering (harness) problem, not a model-capability problem, and lays out three pillars: multimodal model use, harness engineering (skills, memory, token compression), and consistent infrastructure. He also covers observability feedback loops and the need for agent-first auth/trust on the web.

takeaways.what_they_do: Publish per-site skills so the agent observes available tasks before visiting, reusing prior memory instead of rediscovering from scratch each run.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Your agent doesn't have to discover something in the first place if it's done it before. It can use its memory and its skills

takeaways.what_they_do: The harness presents only the optimized, compressed subset of page/tool context needed for the repeatable result rather than dumping everything to the model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The right harness should not only present the right tools, but present an optimized amount of tokens that are compressed

takeaways.what_they_do: Use a smarter model for hard steps and a cheaper model for easy ones, and mix code-writing with direct interaction rather than one model for everything.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Sometimes you'll use a smarter model for a more complex page. Sometimes a a dumber model for a simpler page.

takeaways.technique: Write code instead of clicking (script replay)
takeaways.what_they_do: The most reliable agents intercept network requests and have a coding agent write a replayable script rather than repeating UI actions each time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: The most reliable browser agents that we see in production right now are often writing code alongside using the browser

takeaways.what_they_do: Capture screen recordings, logs, and network activity per run and feed them back so each iteration of the agent improves.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Every agent you run should get better every single time. You need screen recordings, logs, network activity.

takeaways.what_they_do: Guarantee the agent sees identical inputs/layouts across runs; inconsistent rendering causes inconsistent results.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If your infrastructure renders a page in a mobile layout one time and then like in a desktop layout the second time, it's going to have inconsistent results.
